title: 2025 AMC 10B Problem 13
statement: The altitude to the hypotenuse of a \(30\)-\(60\)-\(90^\circ\) right triangle is divided into two segments of lengths \(x \lt y\) by the median to the shortest side of the triangle. What is the ratio \(\dfrac{x}{x + y}?\)

solutions.text: Place the right angle at \(C = (0,0),\) the short leg \(CB = 1\) with \(B = (1, 0),\) and the long leg \(CA = \sqrt3\) with \(A = (0, \sqrt3).\) The altitude from \(C\) to hypotenuse \(AB\) has foot \(H = \left(\tfrac34, \tfrac{\sqrt3}{4}\right)\) and runs along \(x = \sqrt3\,y.\) The median from \(A\) to the midpoint \(\left(\tfrac12, 0\right)\) of \(CB\) meets that altitude at \(\left(\tfrac37, \tfrac{\sqrt3}{7}\right).\) This cuts \(CH\) (length \(\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\)) into \(\tfrac{4\sqrt3}{14}\) and \(\tfrac{3\sqrt3}{14},\) so \(x = \tfrac{3\sqrt3}{14}\) and \(\dfrac{x}{x + y} = \dfrac{\frac{3\sqrt3}{14}}{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}} = \dfrac{3}{7}.\) Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Set the right angle at the origin with legs along the axes (short leg \(1,\) long leg \(\sqrt3\)); find the foot of the altitude and the median line
Intersect the altitude with the median to the short side, then take the ratio of the near segment to the whole altitude
